newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African industry sees falling car sales in 1997.
newsitem.headline: S.African industry sees falling car sales in 1997.

text.p: South African car sales are expected to fall in 1997 following four years of successive growth, the National Association of Automobile Manufacturers of South Africa (NAAMSA) said on Tuesday.
New car sales totalled 249,884 in 1996 against 236,584 in 1995 after a 2.45 percent year-on-year rise in December.
NAAMSA said car sales had finished the year on a "reasonably positive note" but it forecast sales would fall to 242,000 in 1997.

"Trading conditions in the new vehicle market during the first six months of 1997 are expected to remain difficult as a result of general pressure on consumers' disposable income...and particularly the prevailing exceptionally high interest rates," the association said.

Sales of light commercial vehicles in 1997 were seen slightly higher at 132,000 from 129,575 while medium commercials were forecast at 6,000 from 5,457 in 1996. Heavy truck sales were seen at 8,000 from 8,110.
Exchange rate related cost pressures reinforced expectations that new vehicle sales would fall in 1997.
"These pressures are expected to translate into new vehicle price increases during 1997 more in line with the projected rate of inflation as measured by the consumer price index," NAAMSA said.
Increasingly challenging conditions in the domestic market were seen counterbalanced by the industry's growing export business.

Exports of automative components and built-up vehicles were expected to continue in a strong expansionary phase with the aggregate value of components and vehicles expected to exceed five billion rand during 1997 compared to an estimated four billion rand during 1996, NAAMSA said.
